unit: Lorna grew up in Seven Gulls, experiencing severe poverty and devastating family losses, including the accidental death of her brother Julian and her father's suicide. Highly ambitious, she completed two years of study in one at Regent's Academy to become a teacher, hoping to work her way through college. However, her mother coerced her into marrying Rufus Vane at age sixteen to save their farm from foreclosure. Rufus deserted her shortly after, but when Captain Saul brought back a brain-injured man from Havana, Lorna faithfully cared for him for eleven years, believing him to be Rufus. During this time, she befriended Nell Harcourt, though she initially struggled with secret envy over Nell's happy life. When Dr. Hugh Carrow suggested the man could be cured through surgery, Lorna bravely took him to Montreal, where the operation revealed the man was actually Rufus's cousin, Laurence Vane, and that Rufus had died years earlier in Cuba. Freed from her tragic bond, Lorna returned to Seven Gulls and fell in love with author Adrian Treleaven. They became engaged and planned to marry in the winter before moving to Japan.

unit: Hugh Carrow grows up in Brierley and spends three years of his childhood in Alberta with his father. Returning to Brierley School at fourteen, he initially teases Nell Harcourt by calling her 'Carrots', prompting her to break a slate over his head, an incident for which he immediately apologizes. Though Nell holds a grudge, Hugh competes with her academically at school and later at Regent's Academy. After working as a teacher at Pale Sands and a journalist at the Daily News to fund his education, he attends Wexcombe College, where he becomes captain of the Freshman football team, joins the Lambda Theta fraternity, and earns High Honors in Classics alongside the Cooper Prize. Upon learning Nell wishes to teach in Brierley to stay near her foster-mother, Hugh unselfishly withdraws his own application for the Brierley school so she can have it, taking the Pale Sands position instead. Over time, his early romantic overtures are rejected by Nell, leading to a period of distant friendship while rumor links him to Rowena Calder. However, after surviving a near-fatal bout of typhoid fever and completing his medical degree, Hugh's steadfast love for Nell is finally reciprocated. Upon taking over his great-uncle Dr. David Carrow's practice in Seven Gulls, Hugh leases a small white house by the harbour shore. He and Nell are married in the apple orchard at Grey Shutters and settle in Seven Gulls, where they later welcome their son, James Obed (Little Kit).
